groups.description: Who you talk to: personalities, voices, avatars and who may see them.
groups.label: Characters

groups.description: The models and servers DisPatch talks to, and how it finds them.
groups.label: Connections

groups.description: Speech recognition and voices (provided by the voice add-on).
groups.label: Voice

groups.description: Plugins, agent runtimes and the optional panes.
groups.label: Tools & Modules

groups.description: Sign-in, session lengths, and what programs holding the API key may do.
groups.label: People & Profiles

groups.description: Defaults for a new device: theme, language and avatar style.
groups.label: Appearance

retired.characters.default_audience: 4.0: who uses a character is each profile's household list (People), not an audience

settings.description: The address other devices use to open DisPatch, for example https://chat.example.net. Start it with https:// when the connection is encrypted.
settings.label: Public address

settings.description: Turn on when a program in front of DisPatch (such as Caddy or Tailscale Serve) makes the connection secure, so Settings stops warning that it is not.
settings.label: Another program adds HTTPS (reverse proxy)

settings.description: This computer only, or every device on your home network. The setup wizard warns when DisPatch is actually started differently (--host, or BIND_ADDR for Docker).
settings.label: Who can reach DisPatch

settings.description: Shown for information. The address DisPatch really uses is set when it starts (--host).
settings.label: Address DisPatch reports (information only)

settings.description: Shown for information. The port DisPatch really uses is set when it starts (--port).
settings.label: Port DisPatch reports (information only)

settings.description: How often DisPatch saves a quick copy of its database (every 6 hours by default). Off stops it.
settings.label: Automatic copies: how often

settings.description: How many quick copies to keep before the oldest is deleted.
settings.label: Automatic copies to keep

settings.description: Make a complete, locked backup (chats, bots, settings, pictures) on a schedule. The first one makes a recovery key and shows it once: keep it somewhere safe.
settings.label: Scheduled encrypted backups

settings.description: How often a scheduled encrypted backup is written.
settings.label: Encrypted backup interval

settings.description: Older encrypted backups are deleted beyond this many.
settings.label: Encrypted backups to keep

settings.description: Add the media and File Server folders to encrypted backups. They can be large.
settings.label: Include pictures and files

settings.description: The passphrase that locks backups. Leave it empty and DisPatch makes a recovery key instead. DisPatch keeps it for scheduled backups but never shows it again, so keep your own copy.
settings.label: Backup passphrase

settings.description: Where Settings → System reads log lines from. Empty uses <data folder>/logs/dispatch.log.
settings.label: Log file

settings.description: How much the File Server may hold before uploads are refused (20 GB by default).
settings.label: File Server size limit

settings.description: Run the daily clean-up: remove old records, tidy files and shrink the database.
settings.label: Daily clean-up

settings.description: The time of day (HH:MM, local time) the clean-up runs. It waits while a backup is running.
settings.label: Daily clean-up time

settings.description: Forever, or a number of months. Covers every picture DisPatch made: reactions already shown, Image Studio, chat pictures and used picture-set pictures. Pictures still in use are never removed; an old one waits in the trash before it is deleted.
settings.label: Keep made pictures for

settings.description: Used when pictures are kept for a number of months. A picture is old when its last use in a chat and its own date are both older than this.
settings.label: Made pictures: months to keep

settings.description: How long an expired picture stays recoverable before it is deleted for good.
settings.label: Removed pictures: days in the trash

settings.description: Sign-in and usage rows older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Activity log: days to keep

settings.description: Admin audit rows (who changed what) older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Audit log: days to keep

settings.description: Event logs of finished agent tasks older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Agent task events: days to keep

settings.description: Event rows of closed Job Board jobs older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Job events: days to keep

settings.description: Machine upload counters older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Daily usage counters: days to keep

settings.description: DisPatch remembers which agent messages it already copied in. Records older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Copied agent chat records: days to keep

settings.description: Finished, failed and cancelled picture requests older than this are deleted (the picture itself follows the image rule above).
settings.label: Finished image jobs: days to keep

settings.description: Per-day agent usage totals older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Agent spend rows: days to keep

settings.description: Agent approval requests that have been decided, older than this, are deleted.
settings.label: Decided approvals: days to keep

settings.description: Votes and comments on closed Job Board jobs older than this are deleted.
settings.label: Closed-job feedback: days to keep

settings.description: A picture or upload that nothing uses any more moves to the trash only after this many days.
settings.label: Unused files: days before the trash

settings.description: How long a swept file stays in the trash before it is deleted for good.
settings.label: Unused files: days in the trash

settings.description: How many of the newest (6-hourly) quick copies to keep.
settings.label: Automatic copies: recent ones to keep

settings.description: How many daily copies (the last of each day) to keep beyond the recent ones.
settings.label: Automatic copies: daily ones to keep

settings.description: How many weekly copies (the last of each week) to keep beyond the daily ones.
settings.label: Automatic copies: weekly ones to keep

settings.description: An email address (mailto:…) the notification services can contact about your DisPatch. Optional.
settings.label: Push notification contact

settings.description: How long an Admin can be idle before the device signs out.
settings.label: Admins: sign out after idle

settings.description: How long a User can be idle before the device signs out.
settings.label: Users: sign out after idle

settings.description: How long a Basic profile can be idle before the device signs out.
settings.label: Basic profiles: sign out after idle

settings.description: What a device opens after someone signs out, and before anyone signs in: the shared default profile or the sign-in screen.
settings.label: After sign-out, open

settings.description: The profile a device opens after sign-out. It can't be an Admin or have a PIN or password; agent bots and voice cloning are always off for it.
settings.label: Default profile

settings.description: Off, or how many days a device stays signed in when 'Keep this device signed in' is ticked (each use starts the count again). Off signs out every remembered device.
settings.label: Remember signed-in devices

settings.description: Let programs on the DisPatch computer (agents, scheduled jobs) use DisPatch without a key. Turn off once every program sends the access key.
settings.label: Trust programs on this computer

settings.description: What happens when someone opens DisPatch by an address that is not on its list below. 'Allow and list them' lets them in and shows the address here so you can add it; 'Block them' refuses them, which stops a harmful web page from posing as DisPatch. Switch to Block only when the list of unknown addresses holds nothing you use. If you lock yourself out, set host_check: log in security.yaml and restart DisPatch.
settings.label: Unknown addresses

settings.description: Extra names or addresses people use to open DisPatch, separated by commas, e.g. chat.example.net, *.home.example (*. means any name ending in it). This computer's own names and addresses are always allowed. DISPATCH_ALLOWED_HOSTS adds more.
settings.label: Other addresses for DisPatch

settings.description: How much programs with the access key (agents, scheduled jobs) may upload per day, all together, so a runaway agent can't fill the disk. People have no daily limit.
settings.label: Program uploads per day

settings.description: Show a short fixed greeting at the top of each new chat. No AI is asked.
settings.label: Greet new chats

settings.description: DisPatch refuses a few special addresses (169.254.x.x, fe80::, metadata.google.internal) so nobody can use it to reach hidden services. Turn on only if your AI server really is at one of them.
settings.label: Allow special network addresses

settings.description: The hosts Find servers probes for StudioForge, LM Studio, Ollama and OpenAI-style servers, on ports 1234, 8080 and 11434 (write host:port to probe one port). The default is this computer and the compose names studioforge, lmstudio and ollama (a name that does not resolve is skipped). Cloud-metadata and link-local addresses are never probed. host.docker.internal is added only inside a container; see the next setting.
settings.label: Find servers: where to look

settings.description: Inside a container, Find servers also probes host.docker.internal (ports 1234, 8080, 11434), which is the computer the container runs on. Turn off to stop that. It never happens outside a container, whatever this says.
settings.label: Find servers: look on the Docker host

settings.description: The connection a new bot uses when you don't pick one.
settings.label: Default connection

settings.description: An MCP image server for picture jobs, e.g. http://host:8700/mcp.
settings.label: Image server (MCP) address

settings.description: Where finished pictures are fetched from. Empty uses /files/ beside the MCP address.
settings.label: Image server file address

settings.description: DisPatch's own address as the image server sees it, so it can report a finished picture straight away instead of waiting to be asked.
settings.label: Callback address for the image server

settings.description: Let bots make pictures. Automatic turns it on when an image server or picture service is set up.
settings.label: Picture making

settings.description: A command that makes one picture, used to refill picture sets and reaction pictures. Empty turns automatic refills off.
settings.label: Picture tool for refills

settings.description: How long to wait for one picture from the picture tool.
settings.label: Picture tool time limit

settings.description: Image Studio, the Test button and pictures in chat from MiniMax, OpenAI, xAI Grok or a custom server. The Owner can always use them. (A Basic profile also needs Image Studio switched on in People.)
settings.label: Admins: standard image generators

settings.description: Image Studio's Civitai provider, billed in Buzz with no spending limit. The Owner can always use it; the shared default profile never can.
settings.label: Admins: Civitai

settings.description: Image Studio, the Test button and pictures in chat from MiniMax, OpenAI, xAI Grok or a custom server. The Owner can always use them. (A Basic profile also needs Image Studio switched on in People.)
settings.label: Users: standard image generators

settings.description: Image Studio's Civitai provider, billed in Buzz with no spending limit. The Owner can always use it; the shared default profile never can.
settings.label: Users: Civitai

settings.description: Image Studio, the Test button and pictures in chat from MiniMax, OpenAI, xAI Grok or a custom server. The Owner can always use them. (A Basic profile also needs Image Studio switched on in People.)
settings.label: Basic profiles: standard image generators

settings.description: Image Studio's Civitai provider, billed in Buzz with no spending limit. The Owner can always use it; the shared default profile never can.
settings.label: Basic profiles: Civitai

settings.description: The key Image Studio uses for Civitai. Create one on your Civitai account page. DisPatch keeps it but never shows it again.
settings.label: Civitai API key

settings.description: A command that reports free graphics-card memory, so refills wait while the card is busy.
settings.label: GPU status command

settings.description: A booking service that refills ask before using a shared graphics card.
settings.label: GPU lease address

settings.description: Show StudioForge's control panel as a tool on the bar. Needs the panel address below.
settings.label: StudioForge panel tab

settings.description: Where StudioForge's panel is, e.g. http://192.0.2.20:8080.
settings.label: StudioForge panel address

settings.description: The address a phone or laptop elsewhere can open (e.g. a Tailscale Serve HTTPS address).
settings.label: StudioForge panel address for other devices

settings.description: Web search, weather, Wikipedia, exchange rates and a calculator for bots that talk to an AI service directly. Off removes them from every bot at once.
settings.label: Built-in lookups

settings.description: The openclaw program agent bots use. Change it when it is not on the PATH.
settings.label: OpenClaw command

settings.description: How long an agent may take to answer before DisPatch gives up.
settings.label: Agent reply time limit

settings.description: How many agent replies may run at the same time (protects AI models on your own computers).
settings.label: Agents running at once

settings.description: Off: replies are read from the agents' records. Test: connect and compare, deliver nothing. On: replies arrive live.
settings.label: Live agent replies (gateway connection)

settings.description: Automatic uses the live connection when it is up, else starts the agent program. Live only fails a message rather than fall back; Start the program always starts it.
settings.label: How messages reach agents

settings.description: Copy conversations the agents have elsewhere into DisPatch chats.
settings.label: Copy agent chats into DisPatch

settings.description: How often DisPatch checks for new agent messages while they are busy.
settings.label: Copying: check every

settings.description: The longest DisPatch waits between checks when nothing is happening.
settings.label: Copying: longest wait when quiet

settings.description: A conversation quiet for longer than this when first found is followed from now on, not copied from its start.
settings.label: Copying: how far back

settings.description: Which kinds to copy, separated by commas (webchat, main, other).
settings.label: Copying: kinds of conversation

settings.description: A coding agent page (needs the dsh program). Automatic turns it on when dsh is installed.
settings.label: Coding agent (DeepSeek Harness)

settings.description: The systemd user unit that runs dsh web.
settings.label: Harness service name

settings.description: The port the coding agent's screen uses on the DisPatch computer.
settings.label: Harness port

settings.description: An address a browser elsewhere can open for the harness page.
settings.label: Harness address for other devices

settings.description: Show MailForge's dashboard as a tool. Automatic turns it on when MailForge's runtime files are found.
settings.label: Emails page (MailForge)

settings.description: Where MailForge keeps its runtime files. Empty uses ~/.local/share/mailforge.
settings.label: MailForge data folder

settings.description: The address a browser elsewhere can open for MailForge.
settings.label: MailForge address for other devices

settings.description: A client dashboard from another program on the DisPatch computer. Automatic turns it on when its PIN file exists.
settings.label: Clients page

settings.description: Where the client-pipeline service listens.
settings.label: Clients service address

settings.description: A file holding the service's PIN. Empty uses ~/practice/keys/gui-pin.
settings.label: Clients service PIN file

settings.description: The theme a device uses until its user picks another.
settings.label: Default theme

settings.description: The language a device uses until its user picks another.
settings.label: Default language

settings.description: Pictures, or names instead of pictures. Each device can choose its own (Appearance).
settings.label: Default picture style
